modules.title: Introduction to Sources and Methods of History
modules.html:
Oral, written and archaeological sources, and how historians use them. This section covers introduction to sources and methods of history.

Key points

  • The 'Sefuwa Dynasty' is associated with the history of _____. — Kanem-Borno.

Worked examples

Q: The 'Sefuwa Dynasty' is associated with the history of _____.
A: Kanem-Borno — The Sayfawa (Sefuwa) dynasty ruled Kanem-Borno for over a thousand years, one of the longest in history.

Q: The leader of the 1804 Jihad in Hausaland was _____.
A: Usman dan Fodio — Usman dan Fodio, a Fulani scholar, launched the Jihad in 1804 to reform Islamic practice and overthrow the corrupt Hausa kings.

examples.q: The 'Sefuwa Dynasty' is associated with the history of _____.
The leader of the 1804 Jihad in Hausaland was _____.

quiz.q: The 'Sefuwa Dynasty' is associated with the history of _____.
quiz.solution: The Sayfawa (Sefuwa) dynasty ruled Kanem-Borno for over a thousand years, one of the longest in history.

quiz.q: The leader of the 1804 Jihad in Hausaland was _____.
quiz.solution: Usman dan Fodio, a Fulani scholar, launched the Jihad in 1804 to reform Islamic practice and overthrow the corrupt Hausa kings.

quiz.q: The Benin Empire became world-famous for its artistic works made of _____.
quiz.solution: The Benin bronzes (actually brass) were created using the 'lost-wax' casting method and represent high levels of pre-colonial craftsmanship.

quiz.q: The city of Timbuktu became a major center of Islamic learning under the _____ Empire.
quiz.solution: During the reign of Mansa Musa in the Mali Empire, Timbuktu flourished as a center of scholarship, attracting students from across the Muslim world.

quiz.q: The main reason for the British annexation of Lagos in 1861 was to _____.
options: establish a colony for freed slaves
suppress the slave trade and protect palm oil trade
quiz.solution: Britain annexed Lagos to effectively stop the trans-atlantic slave trade and secure the route for 'legitimate commerce' like palm oil.

quiz.q: The Jukun kingdom of Kwararafa was most noted for its frequent military raids against _____.
quiz.solution: In the 16th and 17th centuries, the Kwararafa kingdom (Jukun) was a formidable power that frequently raided Hausa states like Kano and Katsina.

quiz.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 was criticized by nationalists because it _____.
options: gave too much power to Azikiwe
divided Nigeria into three regions without consultation
abolished the office of the Governor
quiz.solution: Nationalists felt the constitution was 'arbitrary' as it was drafted without consulting Nigerian leaders, although it introduced regionalism.

quiz.q: The legendary founder of the Kanem-Borno Empire was _____.
quiz.solution: Historical traditions attribute the founding of the Sefuwa dynasty in Kanem-Borno to the Yemeni hero Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan.

quiz.q: Who was the 'Black Prophet' that led the Sokoto Jihad against the Hausa rulers?
quiz.solution: Usman dan Fodio is the central figure of the 1804 Jihad, though he was a scholar/reformer rather than a 'prophet' in the Islamic sense.

quiz.q: The 'Golden Stool' is a sacred symbol of the _____.
quiz.solution: Legend says the Stool descended from the sky into the lap of Osei Tutu, symbolizing the unity and soul of the Asante nation.

quiz.q: The 'Bula Matari' (Breaker of Rocks) was the nickname given to _____.
quiz.solution: Stanley earned this name in the Congo for his use of force and road-building techniques during colonial exploration.

quiz.q: The Sardauna of Sokoto, Sir Ahmadu Bello, was the leader of the _____ party.
quiz.solution: The Northern People's Congress (NPC) was the dominant party in the Northern Region under Ahmadu Bello.

quiz.q: The headquarters of the African Union (AU) is located in _____.
quiz.solution: Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa, has been the seat of the OAU (and later the AU) since 1963.

quiz.q: Who was the 'Black Prophet' of the Niger Delta who resisted the Royal Niger Company?
quiz.solution: King Koko led the 1895 attack on Akassa to protest the trade monopoly of the Royal Niger Company.

quiz.q: The Berlin Conference of 1884-1885 was held to:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Partition Africa.

quiz.q: Jaja of Opobo was a:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Merchant Prince.

quiz.q: Lagos was annexed as a colony in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: 1861.

quiz.q: Songhai Empire reached its peak under:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Askia the Great.

quiz.q: The Oyo Empire was known for its:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Cavalry force.

quiz.q: The June 12, 1993 election was believed to be won by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: MKO Abiola.

quiz.q: Songhai Empire was destroyed by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Moroccan invasion (1591).

quiz.q: Who stopped the killing of twins in Calabar?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Mary Slessor.

quiz.q: Mali Empire's famous ruler:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Mansa Musa.

quiz.q: Lyttelton Constitution introduced:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Federalism.

quiz.q: Samuel Ajayi Crowther was:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: First African Bishop.

quiz.q: Discovery of Oil in Oloibiri:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: 1956.

quiz.q: The 'Warrant Chiefs' were created by the British to solve administrative problems in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Igboland.

quiz.q: The term 'Biafra' was used by the secessionist state led by...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu.

quiz.q: The 'Warrant Chief' system was used in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Eastern Nigeria.

quiz.q: The Aba Women's Riot occurred in:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: 1929.
